question: Ensuring the resilience of the Union’s food supply is essential for public security and for the smooth functioning of the internal market. Questions have been raised, in this connection, as to how food reserves are being managed at EU level.

Member States may maintain strategic stocks, but limited information is available on the level of coordination and the distribution and accessibility of these reserves throughout Europe. Furthermore, the Commission is currently discussing a proposal for a stockpiling strategy, to be forwarded to the European Parliament also, which makes the need for transparency in this area all the more urgent.
Questions to the Commission: 1.
Does the Commission have, or does it have access to, an overview or chart of food storage facilities in the EU?

Are there EU-wide standards which ensure that food warehouses are strategically located and easily accessible in the event of an emergency (e.g. pandemics, natural disasters, armed conflicts) and what steps is the Commission taking to coordinate, with the Member States, the transparency, interoperability and rapid mobilisation of food reserves in crisis situations?
How will the future EU stockpiling strategy address the monitoring and management of food stocks so as to enhance collective food security?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.11.2025) Member States apply different approaches to strengthen food security preparedness, including the establishment of strategic reserves. The responsibility for such reserves lies primarily with Member States, as this falls under matters of national security.

The Commission does not hold a centralised overview of food storage facilities in the EU, and there are no EU-wide standards defining their location or accessibility. The Commission carried out in 2017 a study on storage capacities and logistical infrastructure for EU agricultural commodities which is publicly available1.

To facilitate coordination in this area, the Commission is supported by the European Food Security Crisis preparedness and response Mechanism (EFSCM)2, which brings together EU institutions, Member States and stakeholders to monitor risks, assess vulnerabilities and exchange best practices on crisis preparedness, including on strategic reserves of agri-food products.

Under the proposed revision of the Common Market Organisation (CMO) Regulation3, this mechanism will be strengthened, and Member States will be required to develop food security and response plans, including regular sharing of information on stocks of agricultural products.

The EU Stockpiling Strategy4, adopted in July 2025, aims to ensure access to essential goods, necessary to maintain vital societal functions, under all circumstances. Agri-food products fall within its scope.

A key action is the establishment of an EU Stockpiling Network with the Member States, to promote information-sharing, best practices and strategic planning and to strengthen cooperation with industry in developing tools for data exchange on critical supply chains and stockpiling.
